task: Describe a bird you can see near your home.
student_text: There is a owl in the tree behind our house. It comes here in the evening, and my sister takes a photo from the kitchen window.

errors.explanation: Use an before a word that begins with a vowel sound, such as owl.

gold.corrected_text: There is an owl in the tree behind our house. It comes here in the evening, and my sister takes a photo from the kitchen window.

english_variant: unspecified; British and American variants accepted

task: Say where you keep a small object at home.
student_text: My keys are at the table drawer near the front door. I put them there after work, so I can find them before I leave in the morning.

errors.explanation: Use in when the keys are inside the drawer.

gold.corrected_text: My keys are in the table drawer near the front door. I put them there after work, so I can find them before I leave in the morning.

english_variant: unspecified; British and American variants accepted

task: Write a short note about a place you like.
student_text: The small bookshop near my school is my favorite place. I go there becaus it has funny comics, and the owner lets me read one before I choose a book.

gold.corrected_text: The small bookshop near my school is my favorite place. I go there because it has funny comics, and the owner lets me read one before I choose a book.

english_variant: unspecified; British and American variants accepted

task: Describe some fruit in a bowl.
student_text: There are much grapes in the blue bowl, but there is only one pear. My brother eats the grapes after lunch, and I save the pear for later.

errors.explanation: Use many with plural countable nouns such as grapes.

gold.corrected_text: There are many grapes in the blue bowl, but there is only one pear. My brother eats the grapes after lunch, and I save the pear for later.

english_variant: unspecified; British and American variants accepted

task: Compare three games that you play with friends.
student_text: We have three games in the cupboard. The treasure game is the most easiest, but the picture game is more fun for my little cousin.

errors.explanation: Use easiest by itself; do not add most to an adjective ending in -est.

gold.corrected_text: We have three games in the cupboard. The treasure game is the easiest, but the picture game is more fun for my little cousin.

english_variant: unspecified; British and American variants accepted

task: Tell a friend about a visit to a farm yesterday.
student_text: Yesterday, my class go to a farm outside town. We see two horses and fed the ducks. Our teacher took a picture, and we ate sandwiches under a big tree.

errors.explanation: Use went, the past form of go, for an action yesterday.
Use saw, the past form of see, for an action yesterday.

gold.corrected_text: Yesterday, my class went to a farm outside town. We saw two horses and fed the ducks. Our teacher took a picture, and we ate sandwiches under a big tree.

english_variant: unspecified; British and American variants accepted

task: Write about a bus ride to a sports lesson.
student_text: On Wednesdays, I wait the number six bus with my neighbor. We ride it to the sports center, where our coach teaches us how to swim safely.

errors.correction: wait for the number six bus
errors.explanation: Use for after wait when you say what you are waiting for.
acceptable_corrections: wait for the number six bus

gold.corrected_text: On Wednesdays, I wait for the number six bus with my neighbor. We ride it to the sports center, where our coach teaches us how to swim safely.

english_variant: unspecified; British and American variants accepted

task: Describe an animal and something that belongs to it.
student_text: The puppy is playing with it's ball in the garden. My brother throws the ball gently, and the puppy runs after it each time.

errors.explanation: Use its to show that the ball belongs to the puppy; it's means it is.

gold.corrected_text: The puppy is playing with its ball in the garden. My brother throws the ball gently, and the puppy runs after it each time.

english_variant: unspecified; British and American variants accepted

task: Compare the size of two bags you own.
student_text: My school bag is more smaller than my travel bag. It has fewer pockets, but it is light and easy to carry on the bus.

errors.explanation: Use smaller by itself; do not add more to this -er comparative.

gold.corrected_text: My school bag is smaller than my travel bag. It has fewer pockets, but it is light and easy to carry on the bus.

english_variant: unspecified; British and American variants accepted

task: Describe the snacks you brought for a day out.
student_text: I packed four sandwichs and two apples for our trip. My friend brought a bottle of water, and we ate everything on a bench by the lake.

errors.explanation: Use the plural spelling sandwiches after four; nouns ending in -ch add -es.

gold.corrected_text: I packed four sandwiches and two apples for our trip. My friend brought a bottle of water, and we ate everything on a bench by the lake.

english_variant: unspecified; British and American variants accepted

task: Ask a classmate to bring something to your home.
student_text: Hi Mia, can you bring your new puzzle to my house after school. My brother wants to play it with us, and I have some lemonade.

errors.explanation: Use a question mark because this sentence asks Mia to do something.

gold.corrected_text: Hi Mia, can you bring your new puzzle to my house after school? My brother wants to play it with us, and I have some lemonade.

english_variant: unspecified; British and American variants accepted

task: Ask someone about the start of a music lesson.
student_text: What time the music lesson starts on Friday? I want to arrive early because the teacher has a new song for our group to learn.

errors.original: What time the music lesson starts
errors.correction: What time does the music lesson start
errors.explanation: For a present simple question with a singular subject, use does before the subject and the base verb start.
acceptable_corrections: What time does the music lesson start

gold.corrected_text: What time does the music lesson start on Friday? I want to arrive early because the teacher has a new song for our group to learn.

english_variant: unspecified; British and American variants accepted

task: Write about what a family member does not eat.
student_text: My uncle doesn't eats eggs in the morning, but he likes toast with honey. He drinks tea before work and takes an apple with him for lunch.

errors.explanation: After doesn't, use the base form of the verb: eat.
errors.type_label: present simple / verb form after do

gold.corrected_text: My uncle doesn't eat eggs in the morning, but he likes toast with honey. He drinks tea before work and takes an apple with him for lunch.

english_variant: unspecified; British and American variants accepted

task: Explain how you travel to your evening class.
student_text: I by bicycle go to my evening class with my neighbor. We leave home at six and pass the fruit shop before we reach the school.

errors.explanation: In a basic statement, put the verb after the subject and the way of travelling after the verb.

gold.corrected_text: I go by bicycle to my evening class with my neighbor. We leave home at six and pass the fruit shop before we reach the school.

english_variant: unspecified; British and American variants accepted

task: Ask a friend to give you a pen for a short time.
student_text: Please borrow me your green pen for the art lesson. I left mine at home, and I can give it back to you before we go outside.

errors.explanation: Use lend when you give something to another person for a short time; borrow means receive it.

gold.corrected_text: Please lend me your green pen for the art lesson. I left mine at home, and I can give it back to you before we go outside.

english_variant: unspecified; British and American variants accepted
